_readme: Scoring rules for Profile Signals. The order of the rules is their priority: they are shown and checked in this order. weight: how much a rule counts in the score. hardGate: true lets the rule alone cap the result: red makes the profile red, yellow caps it at yellow, and an unchecked gate caps it at yellow. enabled: false switches a rule off. Easiest: edit these values in the extension settings tab (right-click the toolbar icon, Options). Saved settings override this file; Reset to defaults there returns to it. After editing this file, reload the extension in chrome://extensions and then the LinkedIn page.

collection._comment: automatic: true (the default) opens More, About this member on every profile you visit, reads it and closes it. That is automated use of LinkedIn's pages; check LinkedIn's terms. automatic: false opens nothing by itself: the dot stays grey until you click Collect now in the panel, or open the About panel yourself.

cache._comment: Collected profiles are kept in this Chrome profile (chrome.storage.local), keyed by the profile URL, so a profile is not collected again until the entry is older than days. Refresh in the panel always collects again. enabled: false turns the cache off.

verdict._comment: Weighted score: green counts 1, yellow 0.5, red 0. Fields LinkedIn did not show are left out of the score. The score sets the color unless a hard gate caps it.

rules.label: Account created
rules._comment: Green if created before 2016, yellow from 2016 to 2022, red if created after 2022. Late 2022 starts the generative-AI era (ChatGPT launched in November 2022): realistic photos, CVs and posts became cheap, and fake profiles became easy to produce at scale.

rules.label: Verifications
rules._comment: Green if LinkedIn shows any verification (identity, workplace, education). None is yellow, never red: many genuine members never verify.

rules.label: Connections
rules._comment: 500+ counts as 500. Creator profiles may show only followers; then this rule is left out of the score.
